theme: A shared household keeps its kitchen stock, shopping, chores and one pantry recipe in Grocy

credentials.admin: admin / admin (ADMIN permissions, created by migration 0027)

seed_command: ./tester-env seed (tester-env-seed.py through the session-cookie object/stock API; also safe to re-run on a seeded instance)
verify_command: ./tester-env verify (login and /stockoverview plus every seeded entity, count, amount, fixed date and rendered page)
notes: All writes go through POST /api/objects/<entity> and POST /api/stock/products/<id>/add with the admin session cookie; there is no direct SQLite access.

Seed wipes only its own business data (products, stock, shopping lists, recipes, chores, tasks and the master data it creates) and rebuilds it, so a re-seed leaves exactly one copy of every seeded record. The migration default rows (Fridge location, Piece/Pack units, default shopping list id 1) are reused, not recreated.

All dates are absolute and fixed (best-before 2026-11-24 .. 2027-10-31, purchases 2026-09-30 .. 2026-11-21, chores 2026-11-23 .. 2026-12-15, tasks 2026-11-05 .. 2026-11-29); no value is derived from the wall clock.

Task due dates are date-only ('YYYY-MM-DD'), matching what the task form's date picker writes. The /tasks statistics widget appends ' 23:59:59' to due_date (public/viewjs/tasks.js:211), so a stored datetime makes moment() return Invalid date and the overdue/due counters read 0 while the row is still coloured red from the server-side due_type; date-only data avoids that upstream grocy 4.7.1 quirk.
Row ids, stock ids and transaction ids are generated by Grocy; assertions key on names, amounts, dates, relations, counts and rendered pages.
TZ=UTC and MODE=production in docker-compose.tester-env.yml; demo mode is not used (it disables auth and generates week-relative dates).

admin-login.evidence: Deploy and verify both POST /login with admin/admin and require the grocy_session_access_token cookie; migration 0027 creates the user, so there is no first-run wizard.

stock-overview-populated.evidence: /stockoverview is the entry page and lists 12 products across 4 locations; verify asserts the page contains 'Stock overview', 'Whole milk', 'Dish soap' and 'Fridge', and /api/stock returns 10 products with stock.

product-master-data.evidence: 6 product groups (Dairy & eggs, Bakery, Produce, Pantry staples, Drinks, Household), 4 locations (Fridge default, Freezer with is_freezer=1, Pantry, Cellar), 5 quantity units (Piece, Pack, Bottle/Bottles, Can/Cans, Loaf/Loaves), 2 shopping locations (Corner Grocer, Riverside Market) and 12 products with fixed names, descriptions, group/location/store/unit, min stock and active flags.

stock-entries-fixed-dates.evidence: 11 stock entries with fixed amount, purchased_date, best_before_date and price; Whole milk carries two entries (3 @ 2026-11-29 and 2 @ 2026-12-06) so FEFO order is visible. Verify compares every entry tuple per product.

stock-amounts.evidence: Amounts are Whole milk 5, Free-range eggs 2, Sourdough loaf 1, Unsalted butter 2, Greek yoghurt 1, Cherry tomatoes 2, Frozen peas 2, Basmati rice 3, Vegetable stock cubes 3, Sparkling water 8, Dish soap 0, Coffee beans 0.

below-minimum-and-out-of-stock.evidence: Greek yoghurt (1 of min 2) and Dish soap (0 of min 2) are below minimum stock; both appear in /api/stock/volatile missing_products. Dish soap has no stock entry, an empty/non-empty contrast in the same overview.

inactive-product.evidence: Coffee beans is active=0 ('delisted when the grinder broke'); it is absent from /products without the inactive filter and cannot be fetched through /api/stock/products/<id>, while the product row and its shopping-list item remain visible by name.

barcodes.evidence: 4001234567890 resolves to Whole milk and 4009876543217 to Free-range eggs through /api/stock/products/by-barcode/<code>.

shopping-lists.evidence: Two lists: 'Weekly groceries' (the renamed default list id 1, so plain /shoppinglist works) with Dish soap 2, Greek yoghurt 2, Coffee beans 1, and 'Weekend market' with Cherry tomatoes 1 plus a note-only item 'Collect the bread order'. Verify compares amount, note and unit per item.

chores-schedule.evidence: 4 chores with fixed next execution dates: Water the herbs 2026-11-23 08:00 (daily, 2 days), Clean the fridge 2026-11-28 10:00 (monthly), Defrost the freezer 2026-12-15 09:00 (yearly), Take out the recycling 2026-11-23 09:30 (weekly, Monday; last tracked 2026-11-17 09:30). The dates come from fixed start_date/log rows, not from today.

tasks.evidence: 2 task categories (Household, Garden) and 3 tasks: 'Order a replacement fridge filter' open and overdue (due 2026-11-10), 'Clean the gutters' open (due 2026-11-29), 'Book the boiler service' done at 2026-11-05 14:20. Due dates are date-only like the task form writes them, so the /tasks overdue counter parses them.

recipe-with-positions.evidence: 'Winter vegetable soup' has 4 servings and 3 positions (Cherry tomatoes 2, Frozen peas 1, Vegetable stock cubes 2) with notes; /api/recipes/<id>/fulfillment reports need_fulfilled 1, missing_products_count 0 and costs 8.10 from the seeded purchase prices.

rendered-pages.evidence: Authenticated GET of /stockoverview, /products, /shoppinglist, /chores, /recipes and /tasks returns 200 and contains the seeded names (verified over HTTP with the session cookie).

deterministic-reset.evidence: Two full reset -> deploy -> seed -> verify cycles plus one isolated RUN_ID=seedcheck/PORT=58088 cycle produced byte-identical canonical state digests (master data, products, stock, entries, lists, chores, next executions, tasks, recipe, positions). Reset + deploy without seed makes verify fail with 'locations are Fridge/Freezer/Pantry/Cellar [Fridge]' (exit 1) while deploy still succeeds.

idempotent-seed.evidence: Running ./tester-env seed a second time without reset leaves exactly the same digest and verify passes; no duplicate products, lists, chores, tasks or recipes.
